summary: Kanai Lal Hazra is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD from the University of Ceylon in 1968 under Sirima Kiribamune and Sukumar Sengupta, later serving as Lecturer in Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 1982).
Kanchu Onoe is a Buddhist studies scholar. Onoe taught as an instructor at Hikone Higashi High School (attested 1963) and later served as a professor at Eizan Gakuin (attested 1976).

Kang-nam Oh specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. Oh studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974) and under doctoral supervisor Yun-hua Jan (attested 1976), later holding a post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).

Kang-yuan Sung specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. Sung completed an MA at the University of Calgary under supervisor A. W. Barber (attested 1999) and teachers Anne Moore and Leslie S. Kawamura.
Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Takamatsu Yoshie and at the University of Paris. Okamoto later held a post at the Tokyo National Museum.

Kanji Tamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts at Rissho University, including as a part-time lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001) and as an associate professor (attested 2026).

Kanoko Tanaka is a scholar in religious studies and Indology who studied under traditional teacher Acharya Tulsi. Tanaka served as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University (attested 2001).
Kansei Tamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1962) and served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1962).

Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Delhi, University of Michigan, and Banaras Hindu University. She founded the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, serving as member secretary, Academic Director, and chairperson.

Karel Werner (1925–2019) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Palacký University Olomouc (PhD ~1949). He founded Masaryk University, served as Dozent at Durham University (1969–1990), and held posts at Cambridge, SOAS, Masaryk University, and Dongguk University.

Karen C. Lang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who completed graduate studies at the University of Washington (1983) under David Seyfort Ruegg. She has held a professorship at the University of Virginia (attested 1991–2026).

Karen Katsumoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a part-time lecturer at Hanazono University (attested 2006) and later held a post associated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) was a religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University. She served as a professor of anthropology at Drew University (~1976–2009).
Karen Nelson Villanueva is a religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies and studied under traditional teacher Geshe Ngawang Dakpa.
Karen Nero is an academic who taught Sally McAra and held posts at the University of Canterbury and the University of Otago.

Karen O'Brien-Kop is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from SOAS University of London. She has held teaching posts at SOAS, the University of Roehampton (attested 2020), and King's College London (attested 2026).

Karin Meyers specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, having studied under Jay L. Garfield. She served at Kathmandu University as an assistant professor and director of the Buddhist studies MA program at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Karin Preisendanz (born 1958) is an Indologist who completed her doctorate and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She taught at the University of British Columbia (1990–1993) and became a professor at the University of Vienna in 1999.

Karl Albert Agathon Benary (1807–1860) was a linguist who studied under Franz Bopp and earned a doctorate from Halle-Wittenberg (1827). He taught at Köllnisches Gymnasium (1833–1860) and served as Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin (1839).

Karl Ammer (1911–1970) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Vienna. From around 1955 to 1970, he served as a professor and Director of the Institute of Indology at the University of Halle.
